title: Autonomous apple fruitlet sizing and growth rate tracking using computer vision
summary: Computer-vision models segment and associate apple fruitlets across days to estimate growth and thinning response. The first arXiv version reports orchard and robotic-field evaluations, with predicted persist/abscise rates within 3% of manual-caliper estimates; this is a measurement result, not a demonstrated yield gain.
ai_technology: Mask R-CNN and pix2pix fruitlet segmentation with an attentional graph neural network for cross-day association
organization: Not stated in the reviewed arXiv v1

evidence.tested: The v1 pipeline estimated fruitlet persistence/abscission rates within 3% of manual-caliper estimates and evaluated orchard growth tracking and a robotic field image set.
evidence.unknown: Results are limited to evaluated sites and varieties; performance does not demonstrate increased yield or downstream agronomic benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Mask R-CNN and pix2pix detect and segment fruitlets; an attentional graph neural network associates individuals across days for growth/thinning estimates.

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 full text, Methods and Results; version-specific figures and chronology checked.
